page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose server belonging to the Dpdsv6 family, powered by an ARM64 architecture. It features a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 4.0 GB per core, a 128 MB L3 cache, and 1890 GB of local storage. The server runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is a key highlight of this hardware profile, with uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth testing in the top 10% tier, alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score. Database operations also rank in the top 10% tier, indicating high efficiency for data-intensive tasks.

The server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff between multi-threaded efficiency and single-threaded execution. While multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang perform strongly, large-model LLM inference prompt processing is poor, landing in the bottom 10%. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for scale-out workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. It is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose multi-threaded applications.
